title: AAP Claims Bhagwant Mann Held Three Hours at Delhi Airport, Fined Rs 50,000
excerpt: The party alleges the Punjab chief minister was delayed on return from a court-cleared Paris trade trip and fined by officials citing 'pressure from above'; authorities have not responded.
body:
• The Aam Aadmi Party alleged on Tuesday that Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann was held up for about three hours at Delhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport on return from Paris and issued a Rs 50,000 challan.
  • AAP Punjab media in-charge Baltej Pannu said officials cited luggage delays, then told Mann they were under 'tremendous pressure from above'; the party did not specify the grounds for the challan.
  • Mann had travelled to Paris for the SIAL food exhibition, October 17-21, after the Punjab and Haryana High Court set aside the Centre's denial of political clearance for the visit.
  • Airport and central authorities had not issued an official response to the allegations in the reports available at publication.

The Aam Aadmi Party on Tuesday claimed that Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann was stopped for around three hours at Delhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport after returning from Paris and was issued a challan of Rs 50,000, Mirror Now reported. The party alleged the action was deliberate and linked it to repeated obstacles it says the Centre has placed before Mann's official foreign visits.

AAP's account

AAP Punjab media in-charge Baltej Pannu made the allegations in a video statement posted on X. According to Pannu, officials initially cited delays involving luggage arriving or being checked. He claimed that when Mann was about to leave after his baggage had been loaded into his vehicle, officials issued the challan, saying they were under "tremendous pressure from above," according to News89's report. "Has any chief minister of an Indian state ever been detained at an airport for three hours in this manner?" Pannu asked, calling the incident an insult to Punjab. AAP leaders including Saurabh Bharadwaj also raised the issue; Bharadwaj invoked Dussehra, saying even Ravana's pride met its end on that day.

""Has any chief minister of an Indian state ever been detained at an airport for three hours in this manner?" Pannu asked, calling the incident an insult to Punjab."

https://x.com/PTI_News/status/2112761988631912955

The party did not specify the reason for the challan. In a separate earlier claim, Shiromani Akali Dal leader Bikram Singh Majithia had said customs officials stopped Mann and his wife, Gurpreet Kaur, for around three hours over suspected excess luggage or money beyond permitted limits, and that the couple was eventually allowed to leave in view of Mann's position.

The trip that preceded it

Mann had travelled to Paris to attend the SIAL Paris international food exhibition from October 17 to 21, leading a state delegation to promote Punjab's products through a Markfed stall. The Centre had denied political clearance for the visit, but the Punjab and Haryana High Court set aside that decision and allowed him to travel, directing that due protocol be followed. AAP also complained that India's Consul General in Paris did not meet the chief minister during the visit, despite the court's direction. According to Pannu, the Centre has denied permission for Mann's foreign visits at least four times.

What remains unverified

These are allegations by a political party about its own chief minister, and they should be read that way. Airport authorities and the central government had not provided an official response regarding the alleged detention or the fine in the reports available when this article was published, and the grounds for the Rs 50,000 challan were not disclosed. What is documented is the friction around the trip itself — a clearance denial, a High Court reversal, and a protocol complaint in Paris. Whether the airport hold-up was routine customs process or something more is a question only the authorities' response, when it comes, can settle.
